name: SOC 2
description: Trust Services Criteria for Security and Availability. Titles are short public identifiers. Descriptions are our own wording, not the criteria text.

requirements.title: Security
requirements.summary: Common criteria that apply to the security of the system.

children.title: Control environment
children.summary: How the organization sets the tone and structure for its controls.

children.title: Integrity and ethical values
children.summary: Leadership sets a standard for honest behavior and people can see it in decisions.

children.title: Board oversight
children.summary: The board, or an equivalent, oversees how management handles security risk.

children.title: Organizational structure
children.summary: Reporting lines and responsibilities for security are defined.

children.title: Commitment to competence
children.summary: People who run security-relevant work have the skills the job needs.

children.title: Accountability
children.summary: People are held to the security responsibilities assigned to them.

children.title: Communication and information
children.summary: How security information moves to the people who need it.

children.title: Quality information
children.summary: The organization uses information that is good enough to run its controls.

children.title: Internal communication
children.summary: Security responsibilities and issues are communicated inside the organization.

children.title: External communication
children.summary: Customers and other outsiders are told what they need to know about security.

children.title: Risk assessment
children.summary: How the organization finds and judges security risk.

children.title: Specifies objectives
children.summary: Security objectives are clear enough that risks can be judged against them.

children.title: Identifies and analyzes risk
children.summary: The organization identifies security risks and decides how significant they are.

children.title: Considers fraud risk
children.summary: The risk assessment includes fraud and misuse, not only external attack.

children.title: Identifies significant change
children.summary: Changes that would affect security are identified and assessed.

children.title: Monitoring activities
children.summary: How the organization checks that controls keep working.

children.title: Ongoing and separate evaluations
children.summary: Controls are evaluated as they run, and by separate reviews.

children.title: Communicates deficiencies
children.summary: Control gaps are reported to the people who can fix them.

children.title: Control activities
children.summary: The policies and activities that carry out the security response.

children.title: Selects control activities
children.summary: Control activities are chosen to address the risks that were identified.

children.title: Technology general controls
children.summary: Technology controls support the security objectives of the service.

children.title: Policies and procedures
children.summary: Policies say what must happen, and procedures say how it happens.

children.title: Logical and physical access
children.summary: How access to systems, data, and facilities is limited.

children.title: Logical access security
children.summary: Logical access to systems and data is restricted to authorized users.

children.title: Registers and authorizes users
children.summary: New access is registered and authorized before it is used.

children.title: Removes user access
children.summary: Access is removed when someone leaves or no longer needs it.

children.title: Restricts physical access
children.summary: Physical access to systems is limited to authorized people.

children.title: Discontinues access as assets change
children.summary: Logical and physical access ends when assets are retired or moved.

children.title: Protects against external threats
children.summary: Boundaries are protected against threats from outside the system.

children.title: Protects data in transmission
children.summary: Data is protected while it moves across networks.

children.title: Prevents malicious software
children.summary: Controls reduce the chance that malicious software is introduced.

children.title: System operations
children.summary: How the organization detects and responds to operational security events.

children.title: Detects vulnerabilities and changes
children.summary: Configuration changes and vulnerabilities are detected.

children.title: Monitors for anomalies
children.summary: System activity is monitored for behavior that is out of the ordinary.

children.title: Evaluates security events
children.summary: Security events are evaluated so the response matches the event.

children.title: Responds to incidents
children.summary: Identified security incidents get a defined response.

children.title: Recovers from incidents
children.summary: The organization can recover systems after an incident.

children.title: Change management
children.summary: How changes are introduced without losing control.

children.title: Manages change
children.summary: Changes to infrastructure, software, and procedures are authorized and tested.

children.title: Risk mitigation
children.summary: How residual business and vendor risk is handled.

children.title: Mitigates business disruption
children.summary: Risks that would disrupt the business are identified and mitigated.

children.title: Manages vendor risk
children.summary: Risks from vendors and partners are assessed and addressed.

requirements.title: Availability
requirements.summary: Additional criteria for the availability commitment.

children.title: Availability
children.summary: Capacity, environmental protection, backup, and recovery testing.

children.title: Maintains capacity
children.summary: Capacity is managed so commitments to customers can be met.

children.title: Protects environmental and recovery needs
children.summary: Facilities, backups, and recovery support the availability commitment.

children.title: Tests recovery
children.summary: Recovery procedures are tested.
